rows.source_location: Research letter text (pages 212-214) and figure legends (Fig 1, Fig 2)
rows.access_level: FULL_TEXT (Ben's PDF; research letter, no tables; Fig 2H bar values are an image and were not read)
rows.design: preliminary (interim) analysis of a randomized, split-body, single-blinded, placebo-controlled trial; one limb 5-FU, the other placebo, both by tattoo-machine microinfusion (MMP)
rows.body_site: limbs (side and which limbs not reported for the group; Fig 2 shows the right leg and left leg of patient number 8)
rows.skin_tone: not reported (one patient named as Fitzpatrick skin phototype III; others not reported)
rows.patients_enrolled: not reported (letter analyses 'the first 8 patients who have completed' the trial; total enrolled not reported)
rows.time_from_last_treatment: not reported for the pooled result (number of sessions not reported; the figure legend shows patient number 8 only, '150 days after treatment')
rows.texture_or_scar: not reported (letter states 'no adverse effects were observed in MMP-treated patients'; texture and scarring not named)
rows.attrition: not reported (only patients who completed were analysed; number who started and dropouts not reported)
rows.citation: Arbache S, Roth D, Steiner D, Breunig J, Michalany NS, Arbache ST, de Souza LG, Hirata SH. J Am Acad Dermatol 2018;78(1):212-215
rows.analysis_unit: limb [per-limb or per-lesion averaging not reported; 8 patients, one 5-FU limb and one placebo limb each]
rows.intervention: 5-fluorouracil microinfused with a tattoo machine (MMP), needling to mild pinpoint bleeding (dose, concentration and number of sessions not reported)
rows.endpoint_definition: repigmentation percentage of IGH lesions measured by Antera 3D melanin quantification
rows.assessment_method: Antera 3D imaging with melanin quantification (operator blinding not reported)
rows.arm_result: 75.3% repigmentation (5-FU) vs 33.8% (placebo), P < .001 [P printed as 'P \.001' in the converted text]
rows.dark_overshoot: one patient (Fitzpatrick III) developed hyperpigmentation areas on both treated limbs 30 days after the intervention, reversed spontaneously within 2 months [limb-level event, so it also concerns the placebo limb]
rows.uncertainty: Follow-up: the time point of the pooled 75.3% and 33.8% results is not reported, and the number of sessions is not reported, so months after the final treatment is NOT_DERIVABLE. The only stated timing is Fig 2's single patient 'before and 150 days after' the intervention [about 4.9 months if that was the only session; not confirmed]. Unit: the letter says Antera quantifies melanin 'in each IGH macule' and Fig 2H gives 'repigmentation percentages of both limbs for all patients'; whether 75.3% and 33.8% are means of patients' limbs or of lesions, and how 'repigmentation %' is computed from melanin, are not reported. No SD, range, confidence interval or name of the statistical test; P < .001 with 8 patients is not explained. Interim analysis of the 'first 8 patients' of a registered trial (NCT02904564) [the arbache2023 record cites the same registry ID, so these 8 patients are probably part of the arbache2023 cohort; count the cohort once]. Internal conflict on safety: the letter says no adverse effects were observed, yet reports one patient with hyperpigmentation on both treated limbs at 30 days. The authors' claim that biopsies at 40 days eliminate postinflammatory hyperpigmentation is the authors' interpretation. Assessment: two blinded dermatologists judged which limb had the best outcome, but that result is not reported; the numbers come from Antera 3D, and whether its operator was blinded is not reported. Conflicts: the first author's 'commercial involvement' is declared, the machine, cartridges and medicines were supplied by Traderm, the authors copyrighted the MMP acronym, and the first author trains dermatologists in the technique. Sessions: Fig 1D says the procedure was 'initially performed only in the central regions of these lesions and was subsequently used to treat the entirety of these spots' [this may mean more than one session; not stated], so 'after the intervention' may not be after the final treatment. Per-patient values in Fig 2H are an image and were not extracted. Partial repigmentation only: no complete coverage or colour-match outcome; skin tone of the group, lesion counts, dose and concentration of 5-FU not reported.
